learner-sex.style: Speak English as a cheerful, polite Japanese beginner at a restaurant entrance, a little loud and happy. Say every word exactly as written: 'sex' rhymes with 'next' and 'checks', an open short 'e' vowel like in 'bed' (/sɛks/), a hissy s at both ends, so a listener clearly hears 'A table for sex, please.' Slightly flat, syllable-by-syllable Japanese-style timing. Natural, not a caricature. Preserve the selected speaker’s vocal identity. Read the supplied text verbatim. Do not add any words or commentary.
learner-sex.note: Take 1 of 4, vowel edited. All four generations (text 'sex' x3, then 'secks') came out with a lax /ɪ/-like vowel (F1 380-455 Hz, F2 1900-2400 Hz; native 'six' F1 ~470, F2 ~1900), i.e. still 'six'. Regeneration budget used up, so the vowel of take 1 (1.795-1.872 s) was moved to /ɛ/ with a Praat source-filter edit (F1 x1.35, F2 x0.92; LPC inverse filter + FormantGrid filter, 15 ms crossfades): now F1 ~600 Hz, F2 ~1750-2100 Hz. wavSha256 is the edited file; the four raw takes are in Drive own-voice/takes/.
